title: How Illinois treated his brother Russell
summary: Cobb says that once Illinois formed his own band he mistreated Russell, who could have been better with proper support, and cites the Polo Grounds game snub.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So after this happened, Illinois left Cab Calloway's AND FORMED A BAND band, and told us we were gonna have a band together. Together. Russell
And once the band got formed, they wasn't together. It was me, myself and I. They fought like dogs, and he treated the boy awful bad. His brother..
Russell was the older. He's the middle, between Linton, who just died in '74, and Illinois was the baby. He's the baby boy ... the baby of all of them, sisters and all.
: Yeah, so my supposition is that
I TRIED TO LOOK AFTER HIS BROTHER WAS ACTUALLY THE REVERSE.
He does; but that's your opinion.
: No, but I had no reason to say that except that Russell, who Roscoe did not appear to be a very wonderful trumpet player, was on quite a lot of his records.
Well, Russell could have been much greater than what he is if he had the right support, and not been hampered by his brother. You know, you can tear a man's heart-strings out.

... and nobody can do it better than a relative. And you know, I get bitter when I think about it, because, see, I wouldn't let nobody do that to me. But Russell loves, and his brother didn't give a damn he loved himself first. You're asking me questions and I'm gonna answer them correct, and as true as I know.
That boy was treated awful. And I think anybody could be torn down so much that your mind gets distorted -- and Russell's mind was distorted.

I could even give you an incident. Illinois was in Long Island and he had an apartment that he maintained down the street from me on 159th or 158th, or whatever it was, but it's just in the next block, across from St. Nicholas, and he let Russell have the apartment. And they worked together.

Now they had a football game going on, over at the stadium over there; where they were playing at the Polo Grounds in New York. He paid money and would take friends because he could afford it, but he wouldn't take his brother to the game.

Does that make good sense? What are you trying to prove there? He's the champ and he's making the money, the biggest money, and he's getting paid as a side man and can't afford it. But he'd take anybody but his own brother.
